rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Thamud received a three-day warning; their faces changed color as Salih escaped with believers toward Palestine before their destruction.
rows.anchor: فأصبحوا في الثاني محمري الوجوه كأنها خضبت بالدم وفي الثالث مسوديها كأنها طليت بالقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hudb hid Salih despite being a polytheist; when tortured followers revealed his refuge, Abu Hudb refused to surrender him, but the people turned to their own impending punishment.
rows.anchor: فنزل على سيدهم أبي هدب لقيل وهو مشرك فغيبه ولم يقدروا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noon cry from heaven, carrying the sound of every thunderbolt and earthly sound, cut their hearts and killed all of Thamud.
rows.anchor: فلما اشتد الضحى أخذتهم صيحة من السماء فيها صوت كل صاعقة وصوت كل شيء له صوت في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a disbelieving crippled woman, Daria daughter of Salaf, escaped the initial destruction; she fled to Wadi al-Qura, reported it, drank water, and died.
rows.anchor: إلا امرأة مقعدة كافرة اسمها دريعة بنت سلف عند ما عاينت العذاب خرجت أسرع ما يرى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report sends Salih and four thousand followers to Hadramawt, where Salih died on arrival and gave the place its name.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خرج صالح ومن معه من قومه وهم أربعة آلاف إلى حضرموت فلما دخلوها مات صالح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Salih died in Mecca aged fifty-eight after spending twenty years among his people.
rows.anchor: وقيل مات بمكة ابن ثمان وخمسين سنة وأقام في قومه عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddī identify the earthquake as the cry.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والسدي: الرجفة الصيحة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim interprets the earthquake as a severe quake.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: الزلزلة الشديدة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses them as motionless, dead, and explains the related word for an animal restrained with gathered legs for shooting, which the Prophet forbade.
rows.anchor: جاثمين هامدين لا يتحركون موتى يقال: الناس جثوم أي قعود لا حراك بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes them as charred, burned remnants like ash, assuming the cry came with burning thunderbolts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه حمما محترقين كالرماد الجاثم ذهب هذا القائل إلى أن الصيحة اقترن بها صواعق محرقة

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī explains the singular earthquake and plural cry by the cry's greater reach from heaven, each wording suiting its cause.
rows.anchor: حيث ذكر الرجفة وهي الزلزلة وحد الدار وحيث ذكر الصيحة جمع لأن الصيحة كانت من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss takes “their dwelling” as their town, using the house as a metonym for the settlement.
rows.anchor: وقيل في دارهم أي في بلدهم كنى بالدار عن البلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “dwelling” is generic, and the fāʾ in “so it seized them” can signal the short interval between their challenge and destruction.
rows.anchor: وحد والمراد به الجنس والفاء في فأخذتهم للتعقيب فيمكن العطف بها على قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an implied warning and three-day wait can supply the antecedent for the fāʾ, so the earthquake follows naturally.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقدر ما يصح العطف بالفاء عليه أي فواعدهم العذاب بعد ثلاث فانقضت فأخذتهم الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction among descriptions of seizure by earthquake, cry, and the overwhelming act: the cry caused the tremor, while each phrase names a fitting cause.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين فأخذتهم الرجفة وبين فأخذتهم الصيحة وبين فأهلكوا بالطاغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “by the overwhelming act” marks cause; the act may be their unbelief or hamstringing the she-camel, and ṭāghiya denotes excess.
rows.anchor: فالباء فيه للسببية أي أهلكوا بالفعلة الطاغية وهي الكفر أو عقر الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overwhelming act may instead mean the earthquake or cry, each of which surpassed bounds.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يراد بالطاغية الرجفة أو الصيحة لتجاوز كل منهما الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence has Salih turn away after the people perish; his speech expresses grief and regret that they would not believe.
rows.anchor: ظاهر العطف بالفاء أن هذا التولي كان بعد هلاكهم ومشاهدة ما جرى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the post-destruction reading, Salih's words let his surviving followers hear his grief, strengthening their faith and resolve to obey God's messenger.
rows.anchor: وليسمع ذلك من كان معه من المسلمين فيزدادوا إيمانا وانتفاء عن معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You do not love advisers” describes their past habit: they did not used to love those who counselled them.
rows.anchor: ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين ولكن كنتم لا تحبون الناصحين فتكون حكاية حال ماضية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view has Salih turn away before the punishment, when they hamstrung the camel and challenged him; their narrative says he left the night before the earthquake.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان توليه عنهم وقت عقر الناقة وقولهم ائتنا بما تعدنا وذلك قبل نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet addressed the people of the Badr well while weeping, saw smoke, and understood that they had perished; it gives their number as fifteen hundred households.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه خرج في مائة وعشرين من المسلمين وهو يبكي فالتفت فرأى الدخان فعلم أنهم قد هلكوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet returned with his companions and settled in their dwellings.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه رجع بمن معه فسكنوا ديارهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports the view that no people were destroyed while their prophet was among them.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: وقيل لم تهلك أمة ونبيها فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Salih left with his followers for Mecca and stayed there until his death.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه ارتحل بمن معه حتى جاء مكة فأقام بها حتى مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for turning away implies despair of their good and certainty that they would perish; the address resembles Noah's and Hūd's warnings.
rows.anchor: ولفظة التولي تقتضي اليأس من خيرهم واليقين في هلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense “I conveyed” is followed by the past “I advised”; “advisers” is general, condemning their refusal of anyone's counsel on any matter.
rows.anchor: لكنه لما كان قوله أبلغتكم ماضيا عطف عليه ماضيا فقال: ونصحت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their habitual rejection of advice arose because their desires overpowered their reason.
rows.anchor: أي ديدنكم ذلك لغلبة شهواتكم على عقولكم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that at al-Ḥijr during Tabūk the Prophet forbade drinking or drawing its water; he ordered the companions to discard cooked food and dough and use the spring of Salih's camel.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزل الحجر في غزوة تبوك أمرهم أن لا يشربوا من مائها

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥazm relies on the report to prohibit ablution with water from Thamud's land except at the spring used by the camel.
rows.anchor: وإلى الأخذ بهذا الحديث، أخذ أبو محمد بن حزم في ذهابه إلى أنه لا يجوز الوضوء بماء أرض ثمود

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet's warning not to enter the punished settlement or drink its water unless weeping, lest the same affliction strike the visitors.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما مر بالحجر في غزوة تبوك قال لأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies a grave as Abū Righāl's: a Thamūd man escaped their punishment in the sanctuary, was struck after leaving it, and was buried with a gold branch that the companions dug up.
rows.anchor: هذا قبر أبي رغال الذي هو أبو ثقيف كان من ثمود فأصاب قومه البلاء وهو بالحرم فسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot was the son of Hārān, Abraham's brother, and was sent to Sodom and the other overturned towns; Ibn ʿAṭiyya instead describes his mission as to a people called Sodom.
rows.anchor: هو لوط بن هارون أخي إبراهيم عليه السلام وناحور وهم بنو تارح بن ناحور

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Lot was sent to a nation called Sodom.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية بعثه الله إلى أمة تسمى سدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lot, when he said” is parsed either with an implied “We sent” coordinated with earlier prophets, or with an implied “remember”; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allow the latter, with “when” serving as the object of “remember.”
rows.anchor: وانتصب لوطا بإضمار وأرسلنا عطفا على الأنبياء قبله وإذ معمولة لأرسلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke, condemnation, and exposure of their disgraceful act; “indecency” means intercourse with men in the anus.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام هو على جهة الإنكار والتوبيخ والتشنيع والتوقيف على هذا الفعل القبيح والفاحشة هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in “the indecency” marks an act whose foulness is familiar and innate, or makes it stand for all indecencies; adultery is indefinite because Arabs often practiced and did not condemn it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا بالفعل معهودا قبحه ومركوزا في العقول فحشه أتى معرفا بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative statement says Lot's people invented the act; “anyone” reinforces total negation and “worlds” broadens its scope.
rows.anchor: والجملة المنفية تدل على أنهم هم أول من فعل هذه الفعلة القبيحة وأنهم مبتكروها

rows.speaker: عمر بن دينار
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn Dīnār says no male-on-male intercourse had been seen before Lot's people.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن دينار: ما رئي ذكر على ذكر قبل قوم لوط

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they attacked strangers because their fertile Jordan lands drew visitors; Satan, disguised as a boy, taught the practice as a way to deter them, and it then spread and became accepted.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كانوا يأتون الغرباء كانت بلادهم الأردن تؤتى من كل جانب لخصبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects restricting “worlds” to people of Lot's own era and rejects construing “preceded” as being first to persist in or witness the act.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن المراد من عالمي زمانهم ومن ذهب إلى أن المعنى ما سبقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The designation “indecency” supports treating the act like adultery, with stoning for a previously married offender and flogging for an unmarried one; al-Shāfiʿī agrees, citing Ibn al-Zubayr's ruling.
rows.anchor: وفي تسمية هذا الفعل بالفاحشة دليل على أنه يجري مجرى الزنا يرجم من أحصن ويجلد من لم يحصن

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik's first view is stoning the offender whether previously married or not, and also the penetrated partner if adult.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: يرجم أحصن أو لم يحصن وكذا المفعول به إن كان محتلما

rows.speaker: عطية وابن المسيب والنخعي
rows.claim: A view attributed to ʿAṭiyya, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Nakhaʿī stones the previously married offender but detains and disciplines the unmarried one.
rows.anchor: يرجم المحصن ويؤدب ويحبس غير المحصن وهو مذهب عطية وابن المسيب والنخعي

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Another view attributed to Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfa imposes discretionary punishment whether or not the offender was previously married.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك أيضا يعزر أحصن أو لم يحصن وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khālid ibn al-Walīd burned al-Fajāʾ for this act under Abū Bakr's judgment; the author says the Companions, including ʿAlī, agreed, and reports later burnings by Ibn al-Zubayr, Khālid al-Qasrī, and Hishām.
rows.anchor: وحرق خالد بن الوليد رجلا يقال له الفجاء عمل ذلك العمل وذلك برأي أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What preceded you in it” can be a circumstantial clause modifying either the people or the indecency, since the phrase contains pronouns referring to both.
rows.anchor: وما سبقكم جملة حالية من الفاعل أو من الفاحشة لأن في سبقكم بها ضميرهم وضميرها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the clause as a fresh rebuke after the initial question, or as an answer to an implied question about why the act should not be done.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هي جملة مستأنفة أنكر عليهم أولا بقوله أتأتون الفاحشة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the bāʾ is transitive in the sense of striking a ball ahead of someone.
rows.anchor: والباء للتعدية من قولك سبقته بالكرة إذا ضربتها قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that transitive analysis: it would make one object cause the other to act, as in striking one stone with another, a meaning that only fits here through a strained metaphor.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التعدية هنا قلق جدا لأن الباء المعدية في الفعل المتعدي إلى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next clause explains the indecency and uses “come to” in the sense of having intercourse; the question is reproachful and rejecting.
rows.anchor: هذا بيان لقوله أتأتون الفاحشة وأتى هنا من قوله أتى المرأة غشيها

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read the clause as an indicative, fresh statement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحفص إنكم على الخبر المستأنف

rows.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya parse “desire” as a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial accusative; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allow this too.
rows.anchor: وشهوة مصدر في موضع الحال قاله الحوفي وابن عطية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ also allow “desire” to be a causal accusative: appetite alone prompts them, without a rational aim such as procreation, making their conduct animal-like.
rows.anchor: أو مفعول من أجله قاله الزمخشري، وبدأ به أبو البقاء أي للاشتهاء لا حامل لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Apart from women” may be a circumstantial phrase meaning apart from them; al-Ḥawfī attaches it to “desire.”
rows.anchor: ومن دون النساء في موضع الحال أي منفردين عن النساء، وقال الحوفي: من دون النساء متعلق بشهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rather” may move to a new account that they exceeded limits, reject their conduct and reproach them, or shift from reporting the sin to judging the excess that produces vice.
rows.anchor: وبل هنا للخروج من قصة إلى قصة تنبىء بأنهم متجاوزو الحد في الاعتداء

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī takes “rather” as rejecting an implied claim that they had an excuse: they have no excuse or proof.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني بل رد لجواب زعموا أن يكون لهم عذر أي لا عذر لكم ولا حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their excess is corrupting overreach: they exceeded customary sexual conduct, with “rather” also allowing an omitted sense, “you did not settle for that.”
rows.anchor: وهي الإسراف وهو الزيادة المفسدة لما كانت عادتهم الإسراف أسرفوا حتى في باب قضاء الشهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle “excessive” marks a settled trait and matches the verse endings in this sūrah; Naml uses a present-tense verb for recurring ignorance and matching verbal endings.
rows.anchor: وجاء هنا مسرفون باسم الفاعل ليدل على الثبوت ولموافقة ما سبق من رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “expel them” refers to Lot and those who believed with him; the later Naml wording supplies the explicit phrase “Lot's family.”
rows.anchor: الضمير في أخرجوهم عائد على لوط ومن آمن به ولما تأخر نزول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's family included his two daughters, Raghwāʾ and Rayfāʾ, and his believing followers; another view says only his daughters were with him.
rows.anchor: وآل لوط ابنتاه وهما رغواء وريفاء ومن تبعه من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun can refer to Lot's household even though they were not just mentioned, because context implies them.
rows.anchor: والضمير عائد على آل لوط وأهله وإن كان لم يجر لهم ذكر فإن المعنى يقتضيهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads “answer” in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن جواب بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw here conveys immediate sequence, as the fāʾ does in Naml and the Spider: the people answered without pause or reconsideration.
rows.anchor: وهنا جاء العطف بالواو والمراد بها أحد محاملها الثلاث من التعقيب المعني في النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their order to expel Lot did not answer his rebuke for indecency and excess; its mismatch resembles Abraham's people answering him by demanding that he be burned.
rows.anchor: ولم يطابق الجواب قوله لأنه لما أنكر عليهم الفاحشة وعظم أمرها ونسبهم إلى الإسراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town was Sodom, named after Sodom son of Bāqīm; Lot migrated with his uncle Abraham from Babylon, with Abraham settling in Palestine and Lot in Jordan.
rows.anchor: والقرية هي سدوم سميت باسم سدوم بن باقيم الذي يضرب المثل في الحكومات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid explain “they are people who purify themselves” as their disgust at intercourse with men and women in the anus.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد يتقذرون عن إتيان أدبار الرجال والنساء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says they only approached women during their clean periods; Ibn Baḥr specifies waiting until women were purified from menstruation.
rows.anchor: وقيل يأتون النساء في الأطهار، وقال ابن بحر: يرتقبون أطهار النساء فيجامعونهن فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another gloss is that they kept themselves apart from the people's sexual practice, close to Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid's first explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يتنزهون عن فعلنا وهو معنى قول ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they bathed after sex and purified themselves with water; the townspeople mocked this as a blame that actually praises.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يغتسلون من الجنابة ويتطهرون بالماء عيروهم بذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they censured Lot's people for something praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس: عابوهم بما يمدح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that their refusal to agree with the townspeople explains the order to expel them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله إنهم تعليل للإخراج أي لأنهم لا يوافقوننا على ما نحن عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the statement as sarcasm about their avoidance of indecency and as pride in filth, like wicked people mocking a pious preacher.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقولهم إنهم أناس يتطهرون سخرية بهم وبتطهرهم من الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Lot and his household, understood either as the believers with him or only his two daughters; his wife Wāhila, a hypocrite aligned with Sodom, was excluded.
rows.anchor: وأهله هم المؤمنون معه أو ابنتاه على الخلاف الذي سبق واستثنى من أهله امرأته فلم تنج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among those left behind” means those who remained in their homes and perished; the phrase explains and confirms her exclusion from rescue.
rows.anchor: ومعنى من الغابرين من الذين بقوا في ديارهم فهلكوا وعلى هذا يكون قوله كانت من الغابرين تفسيرا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the exception already establishes that she was not saved; “among the old” then describes her age, until she perished with her people.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: إلا امرأته اكتفى به في أنها لم تنج ثم ابتدأ وصفها بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural “those left behind” uses the masculine form to include women.
rows.anchor: وجاء من الغابرين تغليبا للذكور على الإناث

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes “those left behind” as those absent from salvation, reinforcing the exception.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: من الغائبين عن النجاة فيكون توكيدا لما تضمنه الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “She was” may mean she became, that this was God's prior decree, or that she remained as she was, with her survival limited to an earlier time.
rows.anchor: وكانت بمعنى صارت أو كانت في علم الله أو باقية على ظاهرها من تقييد غبورها بالزمان الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for raining is construed with the sense “sent,” which explains its use with “upon”; the rain was stones, as other verses describe.
rows.anchor: والمطر هنا هي حجارة وقد ذكرت في غير آية خسف بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The overturned towns numbered five, six, or four; Gabriel lifted them with his wing, inverted them, and stones also struck people away from the towns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت المؤتفكة خمس مدائن، وقيل: ست، وقيل: أربع اقتلعها جبريل بجناحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's wife heard the quake, cried out for her people, turned around, and was killed by a stone.
rows.anchor: وقالت امرأة لوط حين سمعت الرجة وا قوماه والتفتت فأصابتها صخرة فقتلتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is that the stone-rain struck everyone; another view has the towns swallowed and stones striking travelers among them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الإمطار شملهم كلهم، وقيل: خسف بأهل المدن وأمطرت الحجارة على المسافرين منهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says no one survived except a merchant at Mecca whose stone waited forty days until he left the sanctuary; it then killed him, and the people numbered one hundred thousand.
rows.anchor: وسئل مجاهد هل سلم منهم أحد قال لا إلا رجلا كان بمكة تاجرا وقف الحجر له أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have Pharaoh say “your gods,” and the apparent sense is that he worshipped deities himself.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور وآلهتك على الجمع والظاهر أن فرعون كان له آلهة يعبدها

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī says he heard that Pharaoh worshipped cattle.
rows.anchor: وقال سليمان التيمي: بلغني أنه كان يعبد البقر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh worshipped a stone, perhaps a ruby-like object, that he wore on his chest.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان يعبد حجرا يعلقه في صدره كياقوتة أو نحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the possessive mean the gods Pharaoh prescribed for his people, while he declared himself their highest deity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإضافة هي على معنى أنه شرع لهم عبادة آلهة من بقر وأصنام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Egyptians worshipped stars and believed they answered prayers, while Pharaoh claimed the sun had answered him and granted his rule.
rows.anchor: قيل: كانوا قبطا يعبدون الكواكب ويزعمون أنها تستجيب دعاء من دعاها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وعلي وابن عباس وأنس
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Anas, and others read “your deity” in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وعلي وابن عباس وأنس وجماعة غيرهم وإلهتك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One explanation of that reading makes it a verbal noun meaning “your worship”; Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh worshipped but was not worshipped.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان فرعون يعبد ولا يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative explanation is “your object of worship,” namely the sun, called ilāha as a feminine proper name and therefore treated as diptote.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن المعنى ومعبودك وهي الشمس التي كان يعبدها والشمس تسمى إلهة علما عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatened renewed infanticide because he feared Moses; he wanted to reduce the group thought capable of destroying his rule.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يعاجل موسى وقومه بالقتال لأنه كان مليء من موسى رعبا والمعنى أنه قال سنعيد عليهم ما كنا فعلنا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being “above” the Israelites means worldly rank and power; “overpowering” conveys contempt, as if Moses' success could not affect their dominion.
rows.anchor: والفوقية هنا بالمنزلة والتمكن في الدنيا وقاهرون يقتضي تحقيرهم أي قاهرون لهم قهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh also sought to prevent people from believing that astrologers' prophecy identified Moses as the child who would end his kingdom.
rows.anchor: ولئلا يتوهم العامة أنه المولود الذي تحدث المنجمون عنه والكهنة بذهاب ملكنا على يده

rows.speaker: الكوفيون والعربيان
rows.claim: The Kufans and the two Arab reciters geminate both verbs in Pharaoh's threat and its reported execution.
rows.anchor: وشدد سنقتل ويقتلون الكوفيون والعربيان وخففهما نافع

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads both verbs lightly; Ibn Kathīr reads the first lightly and the second geminated.
rows.anchor: وخففهما نافع وخفف ابن كثير سنقتل وشدد ويقتلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Pharaoh's threat distressed them, Moses calmed the Israelites, commanded reliance on God and patience, consoled them, promised victory, and recalled God's promise to give them the Egyptians' land and homes.
rows.anchor: لما توعدهم فرعون جزعوا وتضجروا فسكنهم موسى عليه السلام وأمرهم بالاستعانة بالله وبالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth” may mean Egypt, with the definite article referring to the land they occupied.
rows.anchor: أي أرض مصر وأل فيه للعهد وهي الأرض التي كانوا فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes “the earth” universally as all the world.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأرض أرض الدنيا فهي على العموم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view means the land of Paradise and cites the inheritance of the land in 39:74.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد أرض الجنة لقوله وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “seek help” governs the preposition bi-, unlike “You alone we worship” where it takes a direct object; the prayer “O God, we seek Your help” also uses a direct object.
rows.anchor: وتعدى استعينوا هنا بالباء وفي وإياك نستعين بنفسه وجاء اللهم إنا نستعينك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “The outcome belongs to the God-fearing” can mean victory and triumph.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة للمتقين قيل: النصر والظفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The outcome can instead mean the abode of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations are felicity and martyrdom, or Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السعادة والشهادة، وقيل: الجنة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the phrase means a praiseworthy final outcome for the God-fearing among both Israelites and Copts, all included in God's will.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الخاتمة المحمودة للمتقين منهم ومن القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group reads “He bequeaths it” with a light rāʾ; al-Ḥasan reads it geminated for emphasis, a reading also reported from Ḥafṣ.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة يورثها بفتح الراء، وقرأ الحسن يورثها بتشديد الراء على المبالغة ورويت عن حفص

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read “the outcome” in the accusative, coordinated with “the earth.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي والعاقبة بالنصب عطفا على إن الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' two commands yield two results: seeking God's aid brings inheritance of the land, and patience brings a good end and victory over enemies.
rows.anchor: وفي وعد موسى تبشير لقومه بالنصر وحسن الخاتمة ونتيجة طلب الإعانة توريث الأرض لهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says “the outcome belongs to the God-fearing” is an independent sentence, while “the chiefs said” connects to the preceding narrative.
rows.anchor: هي جملة مبتدأة مستأنفة وأما وقال الملأ فمعطوفة على ما سبقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites' “before you came” refers to Pharaoh killing their sons for fear of the predicted child who would end his kingdom; “after” refers to the renewed oppression.
rows.anchor: أي بابتلائنا بذبح أبنائنا مخافة ما كان يتوقع فرعون من هلاك ملكه على يد المولود

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes “before” as the period from Moses' birth until his mission and “after” as the renewed oppression, forced labor, and abuse.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: من قبل مولد موسى إلى أن استنبأ ومن بعد ما جئتنا إعادة ذلك عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says “after” means Pharaoh's threat and the fears that arose during that period.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والذي من بعد مجيئه يعنون به وعيد فرعون وسائر ما كان خلال تلك المدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the complaint as taxes taken both before Moses' mission and increased after it.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: بأخذ الجزية منهم قبل بعث موسى إليهم وبعد بعثه ما زاد على ذلك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they made bricks and were given straw before Moses; afterward they had to supply the straw, while women spun and wove linen for Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كانوا يضربون له اللبن ويعطيهم التبن فلما جاء موسى غرمهم التبن

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr says they were enslaved from dawn until midday before Moses, then made to work all day without food or drink.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير: استسخرهم من قبل إتيان موسى في أول النهار إلى نصف النهار

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى وعكرمة
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā and a report from ʿIkrima explain the earlier harm as enslavement and killing sons, and the later harm as threats and exile.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى من قبل بالاستعباد وقتل الأولاد ومن بعد بالتهديد والإبعاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the first period as before Moses brought God's promise of rescue and the second as afterward; the complaint expresses doubt and appeal for help.
rows.anchor: وقيل من قبل أن تأتينا بعهد الله بالخلاص ومن بعد ما جئتنا به قالوه في معرض الشكوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī place the complaint at the sea: the Israelites saw water ahead and Pharaoh's army behind and feared capture.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي: قالوا ذلك حين اتبعهم واضطرهم إلى البحر فضاقت صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajallī means manifestation or appearance.
rows.anchor: التجلي الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakk is the verbal noun of crushing and pulverizing; it functions as a passive-participle sense, and dakk and daqq mean the same.
rows.anchor: الدك مصدر دككت الشيء فتته وسحقته مصدر في معنى المفعول والدك والدق بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عزيز
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAzīz glosses dakk as level with the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عزيز دكا مستويا مع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharr means falling.
rows.anchor: الخرور السقوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afāqa means that his senses and reason returned to him.
rows.anchor: أفاق ثاب إليه حسه وعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lawḥ is a board used for writing and other purposes; its root evokes shining, as written things appear upon it.
rows.anchor: اللوح معروف وهو يعد للكتابة وغيرها وأصله اللمع تلمع وتلوح فيه الأشياء المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ornaments include what women wear of silver, gold, jewels, and other precious stones.
rows.anchor: الحلي معروف وهو ما يتزين به النساء من فضة وذهب وجوهر وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuwwār means the lowing sound of cattle.
rows.anchor: الخوار صوت البقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf means grief; the verb is used as “he grieved.”
rows.anchor: الأسف الحزن يقال أسف يأسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarr means pulling or dragging.
rows.anchor: الجر الجذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmāt means taking pleasure in the misfortune that befalls someone.
rows.anchor: الإشمات السرور بما ينال الشخص من المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūt and sakāt both mean silence.
rows.anchor: السكوت والسكات الصمت
